title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper computer-use model
bullets.summary: Released 26 Oct: mid-range model that reads the screen and operates apps (forms, invoices, video edits), priced at $1/M input and $5/M output tokens (half of GPT-5.6 Terra), live in ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Enterprise/Edu and Codex.
bullets.how: The Construct: cheap computer-use option to benchmark against Claude for browser/desktop jobs. PRAGMA: price-drop talking point for operator builds. Brand 9 Signs: maybe for form/invoice drudgery.

bullets.title: Anthropic publishes guidance on folding subagents back into one main agent loop
bullets.summary: Posted 22 Oct (per Releasebot): when subagent splits aren't worth it, with a migration kit and API skills; details not read beyond the changelog line.
bullets.how: The Construct: audit our multi-agent swarms for splits that add cost/latency without benefit. PRAGMA: architecture-review checklist item. Brand 9 Signs: no.

bullets.title: Claude Duet safety post: approval controls and isolated credentials
bullets.summary: Published 23 Oct (per Releasebot): describes approval controls, sensitive-information checks and isolated credentials for the proactive Duet agent, which entered US Pro/Max research preview 21 Oct.
bullets.how: The Construct: borrow the approval-gate and credential-isolation pattern for scheduled agents. PRAGMA: reference design for client guardrails. Brand 9 Signs: no.

bullets.title: Claude Enterprise unifies Chat and Cowork with admin controls
bullets.summary: 23 Oct (per Releasebot): Enterprise plans get combined Chat and Cowork, role/usage admin controls and a new Efficient mode.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: relevant to Enterprise clients deploying Cowork. The Construct: no change. Brand 9 Signs: no.

praxis_lesson: Cheaper computer-use models and leaner single-loop agent designs are converging, so measure each Construct job's cost per task and collapse subagent splits that don't earn their overhead.
